checks.name: Request profile
reads: The User-Agent and the full header set of the request that fetched the page
Client hints (platform, mobile flag, high-entropy values) as sent on the wire
The browser's own navigator values, collected in the page, for the comparison
The browser's timezone, set against the timezone of the IP address

rules.pass: Request and browser describe the same browser on the same platform.
rules.warn: The story mostly agrees but a detail is off: language, platform or mobile hints that do not match the browser, or a browser timezone that differs from the IP's timezone.
rules.fail: No User-Agent at all, an automation or HTTP-library User-Agent, or a request User-Agent that differs from the one the browser reports about itself.
rules.na: The server readings did not arrive, so there was nothing to compare.

checks.name: Proxy indicators
reads: Forwarding headers on the request (for example X-Forwarded-For style headers), separated from Cloudflare's own

rules.pass: Only Cloudflare's normal forwarding headers, or none at all.
rules.warn: Extra forwarding headers are present. That is the finding; this check never fails a run on its own.

checks.name: Datacenter pattern
reads: The ASN organization name Cloudflare reports for the connecting IP
A name-pattern heuristic over that organization name

rules.pass: The owner reads as a consumer or business ISP.
rules.warn: The network owner's name resembles a hosting or datacenter provider.
rules.na: No network owner was reported for this connection.

checks.name: VPN / proxy / Tor intelligence
reads: The provider's flags for the connecting IP: VPN, proxy, Tor, datacenter, crawler, abuser
The provider's fraud score, when present

rules.warn: The address is hosting space or carries an abuse flag: suspicious company, not proof.
rules.fail: The address is flagged as Tor, a proxy, a VPN or crawler traffic, or carries a high fraud score. These are the heaviest network penalties in the verdict.
rules.na: The lookup was off or failed for this run.

checks.name: Managed bot score
reads: The managed bot score Cloudflare assigned to the request
Whether Cloudflare identifies the request as a verified bot (a known, declared crawler)

rules.warn: A score from 30 to 49: the borderline band.
rules.fail: A score under 30, or the request is identified as verified bot traffic.
rules.na: Cloudflare Bot Management is not active on this site, so there is no real score to show. The row says so rather than guessing.

checks.name: TLS fingerprint
reads: The TLS version of the connection
The JA4 (or JA3) fingerprint Cloudflare computed for it, when the plan exposes it

rules.pass: Tells displays the fingerprint but does not score it: on its own it identifies a class of software, not a culprit.
rules.na: Cloudflare did not return a JA4 or JA3 fingerprint for this request, so the row says so rather than guessing.

checks.name: Browser data
reads: navigator.webdriver, the single most direct automation flag a browser exposes
The client User-Agent for headless markers
The plugin list and its internal structure (empty or inconsistent lists are characteristic of headless and patched browsers)
Whether navigator property getters are still the browser's native code
Screen and viewport geometry, touch support against the claimed device class, notification permission state

rules.pass: The self-description is ordinary and internally consistent.
rules.warn: Zero plugins in a Chromium browser, plugin entries that contradict each other, a getter that is not native code, impossible screen geometry, a mobile claim with no touch surface, or a notification permission state real browsers do not produce.
rules.fail: navigator.webdriver is true, or the client User-Agent carries a headless marker.
rules.na: Browser data was not collected in this run.

checks.name: Browser fingerprint
reads: A canvas rendering and its hash
WebGL support, parameters and the unmasked GPU renderer string
The detectable font list and its size

rules.pass: Both probes rendered and hashed normally.
rules.warn: WebGL is unavailable, or the canvas probe failed or was blocked. Real browsers almost always can do both; missing graphics is a property of stripped-down or synthetic environments.
rules.na: Fingerprint readings were not collected in this run.

checks.name: Fingerprint protection
checks.note: Added in v0.3.3 by the fingerprint-protection work (#44, #46).
reads: Canvas: a small solid-colour square, read three times in the page, once in an iframe and once in a Web Worker. An unprotected browser returns exactly the colour that was drawn.
WebGL: the graphics vendor, renderer and limits, read the same way.
Audio: a short rendered sound, three times in the page and once in an iframe, plus a constant signal that should come back unchanged.
Fonts and voices: the installed fonts and speech voices, three times in the page and once in an iframe. A worker cannot read these.
Only counts and yes or no answers leave the page, never the values that were read.

rules.pass: Every surface read steadily, or some were randomized or blocked. Randomized and blocked surfaces are named in the result but cost nothing, because privacy browsers and anti-detection browsers both randomize.
rules.warn: A surface reads one value in the page and another in a worker or iframe. That is what changing only the visible page looks like. A real browser does not disagree with itself.

reasons.note: Scored at 0 points and severity low. It does not change the check row. Privacy browsers randomize too.

checks.name: Fingerprint surfaces
reads: Extension probes against a set of known extensions
Speech synthesis voices
Media and DRM capability, sensor availability, document policy, DevTools state

rules.pass: The surfaces are reported, not scored on their own. Their weight is in combination: each is a small fact, and together they single out one browser in a crowd.
rules.na: The surface readings did not arrive.

checks.name: Performance memory pings
reads: performance.memory samples (used, total, limit) taken alongside the latency pings

rules.warn: At least one sample contains impossible heap values.
rules.na: This browser does not expose performance.memory. Only Chromium browsers do, so Firefox and Safari always read Not available here. That is normal.

checks.name: Worker consistency
reads: navigator.platform and user agent data in the window, a Web Worker, an iframe and a service worker

rules.warn: Any context disagrees with the window about platform or user agent data. One disagreement is enough; real browsers cannot disagree with themselves.
rules.na: Worker readings were not collected in this run.

checks.name: WebRTC network clues
reads: WebRTC ICE candidates gathered in the page (via a public STUN server)
The request's public IP, for the comparison

rules.pass: WebRTC's public addresses agree with the request, or it exposed only local addresses.
rules.fail: WebRTC exposed a public IP that differs from the request IP: the connection claims one address while the browser volunteers another.
rules.na: WebRTC is unsupported, blocked, or produced no candidates. Privacy tools often disable it; that reads as Not available, not as a failure.

checks.name: Latency
reads: The median browser-to-edge fetch time measured in the page
Cloudflare's TCP (and QUIC, when present) round-trip times for the connection

rules.warn: The browser's measured latency is far higher than the handshake's: something (a remote browser, a relay, an extra hop) is between the page and the connection it arrived on.
rules.na: No browser or TCP round-trip time was returned.

checks.name: Remote-control tells
checks.note: The row shipped in v0.2.0. prototype_lie_mismatch was added on master: Function.prototype.toString and the navigator.webdriver, languages, and plugins getters are read in the page, a same-origin iframe, and a Web Worker, and a disagreement is scored. A patch that looks the same in every context keeps its existing reason and points.
reads: Known automation globals on window and driver keys on document
A CDP serialization probe (a known side channel of the DevTools protocol)
Whether the webdriver getter is native, and whether the property was redefined to hide
Whether everyday native functions (Function.prototype.toString, permissions.query) have been replaced by script
Whether Function.prototype.toString and the navigator.webdriver, languages, and plugins getters agree across the page, a same-origin iframe, and a Web Worker
Input event trust: scripted events anywhere on the page, the interaction test's typing and clicks included, and events while the document is hidden or unfocused
Impossible window geometry (a zero outer size)

rules.pass: No machinery found and no patch seams showing.
rules.warn: The CDP probe tripped, everyday functions were replaced by script, Function.prototype.toString or a navigator getter disagrees across contexts, or trusted input arrived while the page lacked focus.
rules.fail: Driver globals or document keys found, scripted input, input into a hidden page, a zero-size window, or evidence the webdriver flag was hidden by patching. These are the most specific findings in the whole report.
rules.na: Remote-control readings were not collected in this run.

reasons.note: Scores only when the page, iframe, and Worker disagree. 15 points, medium, same weight as native_function_patched, and it does not replace that reason.

checks.name: Behavioural classification
checks.note: The row shipped in v0.2.0. behavior_evidence_invalid was added in v0.3.3 when the Worker started deriving the behaviour score (#35, #38).
reads: Pointer, keyboard, scroll, focus and visibility events and their timing during the visit
The activity from the interaction test, when taken

rules.pass: A score of 0.5 or better. A short, still visit scores lower than an active one; that is the measure working, not an accusation.
rules.warn: A score from 0.25 to 0.5: borderline texture.
rules.fail: A behaviour score under 0.25, or evidence that is missing or does not hold together.
rules.na: Behaviour evidence was not collected in this run.

checks.name: Interaction
checks.note: The interaction row shipped in v0.3.0 with 13 checks. int_focus and int_visibility were added in v0.3.3 (#19, #40). While the checks are uncalibrated, a raw fail scores medium at 3 points and a raw warn scores low at 1 point, so the row warns and does not fail.
reads: The order of press and release events on the Start and Submit buttons
Whether each button was pressed with the pointer, or with Enter or Space from the keyboard. A keyboard press has no pointer position, so the pointer checks are not judged for it
Where on each button the pointer landed, and the offset between screen and window coordinates
How far the pointer travelled in the second before each press, counted in pixels, never as a path
How long each press and each key was held, and the gaps between keys
Whether the text arrived as typed keys, as pasted text, or as text with no key presses
Whether the phrase field was focused by the click or the key before typing, and whether blur and focus arrived in order around Start and Submit
Whether trusted input arrived while the tab was hidden or the page was unfocused
How long the task took from Start to Submit

rules.pass: The task was completed and the evidence matched a person.
rules.warn: The task was completed and something was unusual, such as a paste, a missing key event, screen coordinates equal to window coordinates on every click, focus that did not come from the click or key, or input while the tab was hidden.
rules.na: The task was not taken, or no check could be judged on it. That is a neutral result; the verdict is computed without it.

reasons.note: Adds no points when synthetic_input has already scored for the same script-made events. The status is still recorded.
Scored when a posted interaction report does not match its schema. It is not one of the int_* checks.
